target_customer: Employee benefits brokerages (and their employer clients) that need to educate employees about plan choices
problem: Employees misunderstand benefits and choose plans poorly; brokers educate with PDFs and slide decks.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to brokerages, with a carrier funded access pricing option
product_category: Benefits education and decision support software

founders.name: Ben Hale
founders.background_notes: Named CEO and one of four founders by TechBuzz (2021-10).

founders.name: Landon Fielding
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him Founder/CEO; TechBuzz names Ben Hale as CEO. Conflict unresolved.

competitors.name: Employee Navigator
competitors.what: Benefits administration and enrollment platform; Brite calls itself the Employee Navigator of benefits education

competitors.name: PDFs and PowerPoint decks
competitors.what: Status quo broker benefit guides; the CEO says this is the real competition

technical_complexity.rationale: Turns plan documents into mobile guides with decision support; mostly standard web engineering and content ingestion.

defensibility.rationale: Broker book workflows and carrier funded distribution create stickiness, but the product category has established vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Brite raised a Series A in 2022 and stayed independent.

market_need_then: Brokers relied on static documents; Brite later reported over 3 million employees reached (company claim) and partners such as USI, Gallagher and Aon, indicating demand from large brokerages.

branding.domain_note: Uses britebenefits.com; other companies named Brite (Brite Payments, Brite Drinks) exist.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and helpful: Guide employees to better benefit decisions.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press and broker partnerships only; the name is shared by unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Brite sold benefits education guides to brokerages, raised a $1.5M seed after YC in October 2021 and a $7.8M Series A led by Elevation Capital in July 2022. It now lists large brokerage partners and reports over 3 million employees reached, so it appears to have a working sales motion in a niche. No exit or distress was found.
notes: The Series A page (siliconslopes) could not be opened because the host did not resolve; the round is taken from its search result summary and corroborated by CB Insights style listings in search results. Totals raised differ across aggregators ($9.4M to $9.56M). Founder education and prior employers were not found. Jellyvision and Benefitfocus are plausible rivals but no source dated near the batch was found for them.
